title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第四十七 良吏
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第四十七 良吏 Volume 53: Good Officials

sentences.zh: 昔漢宣帝以爲「政平訟理，其惟良二千石乎！

translations.literal: In antiquity Han Emperor Xuan held that "When government is level and lawsuits are settled, is this not the work of good two-thousand-bushel officials!"
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Han Emperor Xuan said, "When government is level and lawsuits are settled, is this not the work of good two-thousand-bushel officials!"

sentences.zh: 」前史亦云：「今之郡守，古之諸侯也。

translations.literal: " The earlier histories also say: "Today's prefectural administrators are the feudal lords of old.
translations.idiomatic: " the earlier histories also say, "Today's prefects are the feudal lords of old.

sentences.zh: 」故長吏之職，號爲親民，是以導德齊禮，移風易俗，咸必由之。

translations.literal: " Therefore the office of chief administrators is called "bringing close to the people"; hence to guide virtue, equalize ritual, shift custom, and change habit—all must pass through them.
translations.idiomatic: " therefore the office of chief administrator is called "bringing close to the people"; guiding virtue, equalizing ritual, shifting custom, and changing habit—all must pass through them.

sentences.zh: 齊末昏亂，政移羣小，賦調雲起，徭役無度。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi, amid disorder, government passed to petty men; levies and taxes rose like clouds; corvée labor knew no limits.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qi, amid disorder, government passed to petty men; levies piled up like clouds and corvée knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 守宰多倚附權門，互長貪虐，掊克聚斂，侵愁細民，天下搖動，無所厝其手足。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates mostly leaned on powerful cliques, each feeding greed and cruelty, squeezing and hoarding wealth, pressing and anguishing the common folk—the realm trembled, and nowhere could people place hands and feet.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates leaned on powerful cliques, fed one another's greed and cruelty, squeezed and hoarded, and pressed the common folk until the realm shook and people had nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 高祖在田，知民疾苦，及梁臺建，仍下寬大之書，昏時雜調，咸悉除省，於是四海之內，始得息肩。

translations.literal: While Gaozu was still in the fields he knew the people's toil and pain; when the Liang platform was established he issued writs of leniency, abolishing every miscellaneous exaction of the dark age—within the four seas people at last could rest their shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was still in the fields he knew the people's suffering; when the Liang regime was established he issued writs of leniency and abolished every miscellaneous levy of the dark age—within the four seas people at last could breathe easier.

sentences.zh: 逮踐皇極，躬覽庶事，日昃聽政，求民之瘼。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne he personally reviewed myriad affairs, hearing governance until sundown, seeking the people's sores.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne he personally reviewed myriad affairs, hearing governance past sundown and seeking the people's wounds.

sentences.zh: 乃命輶軒以省方俗，置肺石以達窮民，務加隱卹，舒其急病。

translations.literal: He ordered touring carriages to inspect regional customs, set up the grievance stone to reach the destitute, strove to add hidden succor, and ease their urgent distress.
translations.idiomatic: He sent touring carriages to inspect regional customs, set up the grievance stone so the destitute could be heard, strove to add hidden relief, and ease urgent distress.

sentences.zh: 元年，始去人貲，計丁爲布；

translations.literal: In the first year he first abolished the household-asset tax, counting males for cloth levies;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year he abolished the household-asset tax and counted males for cloth levies;

sentences.zh: 身服浣濯之衣，御府無文飾，宮掖不過綾彩，無珠璣錦繡；

translations.literal: he himself wore washed clothes; the imperial storehouse had no ornamental trim; the palace women wore no more than figured silk—no pearls, gems, brocade, or embroidery;
translations.idiomatic: he himself wore washed clothes; the imperial storehouse had no ornament; palace women wore no more than figured silk—no pearls, gems, brocade, or embroidery;

sentences.zh: 太官撤牢饌，每日膳菜蔬，飲酒不過三盞：以儉先海內。

translations.literal: the Grand Steward withdrew lavish banquets—daily meals were vegetables, wine limited to three cups: taking frugality ahead of all within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Steward withdrew lavish banquets—daily meals were vegetables and wine was limited to three cups: taking frugality ahead of all within the seas.

sentences.zh: 每選長吏，務簡廉平，皆召見御前，親勗治道。

translations.literal: Whenever choosing chief administrators he sought simplicity, integrity, and fairness—each was summoned before the throne and personally urged in the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he chose chief administrators he sought simplicity, integrity, and fairness—each was summoned before the throne and personally urged in the way of governance.

sentences.zh: 始擢尚書殿中郎到溉爲建安內史，左民侍郎劉鬷爲晉安太守，溉等居官，並以廉潔著。

translations.literal: At first he promoted Attendant in the Secretariat Inner Section Dao Gai to Internal Administrator of Jian'an, and Left People Section Director Liu Zong to Administrator of Jin'an—Gai and the others in office all became known for pure integrity.
translations.idiomatic: At first he promoted Attendant in the Secretariat Inner Section Dao Gai to internal administrator of Jian'an and Left People Section Director Liu Zong to administrator of Jin'an—Gai and the others in office all became known for pure integrity.

sentences.zh: 又著令：小縣有能，遷爲大縣；

translations.literal: He also issued an ordinance: if a small county magistrate showed ability, transfer him to a large county;
translations.idiomatic: He also issued an ordinance: if a small county magistrate showed ability, transfer him to a large county;

sentences.zh: 大縣有能，遷爲二千石。

translations.literal: if a large county magistrate showed ability, promote him to two-thousand-bushel rank.
translations.idiomatic: if a large county magistrate showed ability, promote him to two-thousand-bushel rank.

sentences.zh: 於是山陰令丘仲孚治有異績，以爲長沙內史；

translations.literal: Thus Shanyin Magistrate Qiu Zhongfu, whose governance showed extraordinary merit, was made Internal Administrator of Changsha;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Shanyin Magistrate Qiu Zhongfu, whose governance showed extraordinary merit, was made internal administrator of Changsha;

sentences.zh: 武康令何遠清公，以爲宣城太守。

translations.literal: Wukang Magistrate He Yuan, pure and fair, was made Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wukang Magistrate He Yuan, pure and fair, was made administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 剖符爲吏者，往往承風焉。

translations.literal: Those who received tally seals as administrators often took up the wind accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Those who received tally seals as administrators often followed suit.

sentences.zh: 若新野庾蓽諸任職者，以經術潤飾吏政，或所居流惠，或去後見思，蓋後來之良吏也。

translations.literal: Such as Yu Bi of Xinye and others who took office—using classical learning to polish administration, some leaving flowing grace in their tenure, some missed after departing—were indeed the good officials of later times.
translations.idiomatic: Such as Yu Bi of Xinye and others who took office—using classical learning to polish administration, some leaving grace in their tenure, some missed after departing—were the good officials of later times.

sentences.zh: 綴爲《良吏篇》云。

translations.literal: They are collected in this "Biography of Good Officials."
translations.idiomatic: They are collected in this Biography of Good Officials.

sentences.zh: 庾蓽字休野，新野人也。

translations.literal: Yu Bi, styled Xiuye, was a man of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bi, styled Xiuye, came from Xinye.

sentences.zh: 父深之，宋應州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Shenzhi was Song Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shenzhi was Song inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 蓽年十歲，遭父憂，居喪毀瘠，爲州黨所稱。

translations.literal: At ten Bi suffered his father's death; in mourning he wasted and withered, praised by the province and district.
translations.idiomatic: At ten Bi lost his father; in mourning he wasted away, praised by the province and district.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，爲州迎主簿，舉秀才，累遷安西主簿、尚書殿中郎、驃騎功曹史。

translations.literal: At his capping he became the province's Chief Clerk for Reception, was recommended as Cultivated Talent, and rose through Western Pacification Army Chief Clerk, Attendant in the Secretariat Inner Section, and Merit Officer in the Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping he became the province's chief clerk for reception, was recommended as Cultivated Talent, and rose through Western Pacification Army chief clerk, Attendant in the Secretariat Inner Section, and merit officer in the Rapid Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 博涉羣書，有口辯。

translations.literal: He ranged broadly through books and had skill in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged broadly through books and had skill in debate.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，與魏和親，以蓽兼散騎常侍報使，還拜散騎侍郎，知東宮管記事。

translations.literal: In Qi Yongming, when peace was made with Wei, Bi was additionally made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry on the return mission; on return he was appointed Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and managed the Eastern Palace record-keeping.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Yongming, when peace was made with Wei, Bi was additionally made Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry on the return mission; on return he was appointed Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and managed Eastern Palace records.

sentences.zh: 鬱林王卽位廢，掌中書詔誥，出爲荊州別駕。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yulin was enthroned and then deposed, he managed Secretariat edicts; he went out as Vice Administrator of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yulin was enthroned and then deposed, he managed Secretariat edicts; he went out as vice administrator of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 仍遷西中郎諮議參軍，復爲州別駕。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Army Adviser of the Western Middle General, again serving as Vice Administrator of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to army adviser of the Western Middle General, again serving as vice administrator of the province.

sentences.zh: 前後綱紀，皆致富饒。

translations.literal: His predecessors in managing the province all grew rich.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessors in managing the province all grew rich.

sentences.zh: 蓽再爲之，清身率下，杜絕請託，布被蔬食，妻子不免饑寒。

translations.literal: Bi twice held the post—purifying himself and leading subordinates, cutting off all entreaties, hemp bedding and vegetable fare; wife and children still knew hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Bi twice held the post—purifying himself and leading subordinates, cutting off all entreaties, with hemp bedding and vegetable fare; wife and children still knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 明帝聞而嘉焉，手敕褒美，州里榮之。

translations.literal: Mingdi heard and praised him, personally decreeing commendation—the province and district honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi heard and praised him, personally decreeing commendation—the province and district honored him.

sentences.zh: 沈瑀字伯瑜，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Yu, styled Boyu, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yu, styled Boyu, came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 叔父昶，事宋建平王景素，景素謀反，昶先去之；

translations.literal: His uncle Chang served Song Prince of Jianping Jing Su; when Jing Su plotted rebellion, Chang left him first;
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Chang served Song Prince of Jianping Jing Su; when Jing Su plotted rebellion, Chang left him first;

sentences.zh: 及敗，坐繫獄，瑀詣臺陳請，得免罪，由是知名。

translations.literal: when the plot failed he was imprisoned; Yu went to the capital to plead and secured release—by this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: when the plot failed he was imprisoned; Yu went to the capital to plead and secured release—by this he became known.

sentences.zh: 起家州從事、奉朝請。

translations.literal: He began his career as Province Attendant and Bearer of the Court Greeting.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as province attendant and bearer of the court greeting.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣齊尚書右丞殷濔，濔與語及政事，甚器之，謂曰：「觀卿才幹，當居吾此職。

translations.literal: Once he called on Qi Right Director in the Secretariat Yin Mi; Mi spoke with him on governance and greatly valued him, saying: "Judging your talent, you should hold this office of mine.
translations.idiomatic: Once he called on Qi Right Director in the Secretariat Yin Mi; Mi spoke with him on governance and greatly valued him, saying, "Judging your talent, you should hold this office of mine.

sentences.zh: 」司徒、竟陵王子良聞瑀名，引爲府參軍，領揚州部傳從事。

translations.literal: " Minister of Works and Prince of Jingling Zi Liang heard Yu's name and brought him in as a staff officer, concurrently leading Yangzhou's relay and transport duties.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Works and Prince of Jingling Zi Liang heard Yu's name and brought him in as a staff officer, concurrently leading Yangzhou relay and transport duties.

sentences.zh: 時建康令沈徽孚恃勢陵瑀，瑀以法繩之，衆憚其強。

translations.literal: At the time Jiankang Magistrate Shen Zhengfu relied on power to insult Yu; Yu bound him with law—all feared his strength.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jiankang Magistrate Shen Zhengfu relied on power to insult Yu; Yu bound him with law—all feared his strength.

sentences.zh: 子良甚相知賞，雖家事皆以委瑀。

translations.literal: Zi Liang knew and prized him deeply; even household affairs he entrusted entirely to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Liang knew and prized him deeply; even household affairs he entrusted entirely to Yu.

sentences.zh: 子良薨，瑀復事刺史、始安王遙光。

translations.literal: When Zi Liang died, Yu again served the Inspector, Prince of Shi'an Yao Guang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zi Liang died, Yu again served the inspector, Prince of Shi'an Yao Guang.

sentences.zh: 嘗被使上民丁，速而無怨。

translations.literal: Once sent to register household males for corvée, he was swift and without complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Once sent to register household males for corvée, he was swift and without complaint.

sentences.zh: 遙光謂同使曰：「爾何不學沈瑀所爲？

translations.literal: Yao Guang said to his fellow envoys: "Why do you not learn from what Shen Yu does?"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guang said to his fellow envoys, "Why do you not learn from what Shen Yu does?"

sentences.zh: 」乃令專知州獄事。

translations.literal: " He then had Yu solely manage the province's prison affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " he then had Yu solely manage the province's prison affairs.

sentences.zh: 湖熟縣方山埭高峻，冬月，公私行侶以爲艱難，明帝使瑀行治之。

translations.literal: Hushu County's Fangshan dam was steep and high; in winter months travelers public and private found it arduous—Mingdi sent Yu to go and repair it.
translations.idiomatic: Hushu County's Fangshan dam was steep and high; in winter travelers public and private found it arduous—Mingdi sent Yu to repair it.

sentences.zh: 瑀乃開四洪，斷行客就作，三日立辦。

translations.literal: Yu opened four sluices and halted travelers until they worked—within three days it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Yu opened four sluices and halted travelers until they worked—within three days it was finished.

sentences.zh: 揚州書佐私行，詐稱州使，不肯就作，瑀鞭之三十。

translations.literal: A Yangzhou clerical aide traveled privately, falsely claiming to be a provincial envoy, and refused to work—Yu flogged him thirty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: A Yangzhou clerical aide traveled privately, falsely claiming to be a provincial envoy, and refused to work—Yu flogged him thirty strokes.

sentences.zh: 書佐歸訴遙光，遙光曰：「沈瑀必不枉鞭汝。

translations.literal: The clerk returned and complained to Yao Guang; Yao Guang said: "Shen Yu would surely not wrongly flog you.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk returned and complained to Yao Guang; Yao Guang said, "Shen Yu would surely not wrongly flog you.

sentences.zh: 」覆之，果有詐。

translations.literal: " On reinvestigation there was indeed fraud.
translations.idiomatic: " on reinvestigation there was indeed fraud.

sentences.zh: 明帝復使瑀築赤山塘，所費減材官所量數十萬，帝益善之。

translations.literal: Mingdi again had Yu build Chishan Pond—the expense was reduced by several hundred thousand from what the Works Bureau estimated, and the Emperor prized him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi again had Yu build Chishan Pond—the expense fell several hundred thousand below the Works Bureau estimate, and the Emperor prized him all the more.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，爲建德令，教民一丁種十五株桑、四株柿及梨栗，女丁半之，人咸歡悅，頃之成林。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was Magistrate of Jiande; he taught each male to plant fifteen mulberry trees, four persimmon trees, and pear and chestnut trees—female workers half as much—all rejoiced, and shortly groves were formed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai he was magistrate of Jiande; he taught each male to plant fifteen mulberry trees, four persimmon trees, and pear and chestnut trees—female workers half as much—all rejoiced, and shortly groves were formed.

sentences.zh: 去官還京師，兼行選曹郎。

translations.literal: Leaving office he returned to the capital and concurrently served as an officer in the Selection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving office he returned to the capital and concurrently served as an officer in the Selection Bureau.

sentences.zh: 隨陳伯之軍至江州，會義師圍郢城，瑀說伯之迎高祖。

translations.literal: Following Chen Bozhi's army to Jiangzhou, when the righteous army besieged Yingcheng, Yu persuaded Bozhi to welcome Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Following Chen Bozhi's army to Jiangzhou, when the righteous army besieged Yingcheng, Yu persuaded Bozhi to welcome Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 伯之泣曰：「余子在都，不得出城，不能不愛之。

translations.literal: Bozhi wept and said: "My sons are in the capital and cannot leave the city—I cannot but love them.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi wept and said, "My sons are in the capital and cannot leave the city—I cannot but love them.

sentences.zh: 」瑀曰：「不然，人情匈匈，皆思改計，若不早圖，衆散難合。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "Not so—the mood is turbulent and all wish to change course; if you do not plan early, when the host disperses it will be hard to reunite.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu said, "Not so—the mood is turbulent and all wish to change course; if you do not plan early, when the host disperses it will be hard to reunite.

sentences.zh: 」伯之遂舉衆降，瑀從在高祖軍中。

translations.literal: " Bozhi then raised his host in surrender, and Yu followed in Gaozu's army.
translations.idiomatic: " Bozhi then raised his host in surrender, and Yu followed in Gaozu's army.

sentences.zh: 初，瑀在竟陵王家，素與范雲善。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Yu was in the Prince of Jingling's household, he had long been close to Fan Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Yu was in the Prince of Jingling's household, he had long been close to Fan Yun.

sentences.zh: 齊末，嘗就雲宿，夢坐屋梁柱上，仰見天中有字曰「范氏宅」。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi he once stayed overnight with Yun and dreamed he sat atop a house beam and pillar, looking up to see characters in the sky reading "Fan's residence."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qi he once stayed overnight with Yun and dreamed he sat atop a house beam and pillar, looking up to see characters in the sky reading "Fan's residence."

sentences.zh: 至是，瑀爲高祖說之。

translations.literal: At this time Yu told this dream to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Yu told this dream to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「雲得不死，此夢可驗。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "If Yun does not die, this dream may be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "If Yun does not die, this dream may be verified.

sentences.zh: 」及高祖卽位，雲深薦瑀，自暨陽令擢兼尚書右丞。

translations.literal: " When Gaozu took the throne, Yun deeply recommended Yu, promoting him from Magistrate of Jiyang to Concurrent Right Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " when Gaozu took the throne, Yun deeply recommended Yu, promoting him from magistrate of Jiyang to concurrent Right Director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時天下初定，陳伯之表瑀催督運轉，軍國獲濟，高祖以爲能。

translations.literal: When the realm was first settled, Chen Bozhi memorialized that Yu hastened transport and supply—the army and state were sustained; Gaozu held him capable.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was first settled, Chen Bozhi memorialized that Yu hastened transport and supply—the army and state were sustained; Gaozu held him capable.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書駕部郎，兼右丞如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Master of Carriages in the Secretariat, concurrently Right Director as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Master of Carriages in the Secretariat, concurrently Right Director as before.

sentences.zh: 瑀薦族人沈僧隆、僧照有吏幹，高祖並納之。

translations.literal: Yu recommended his clansmen Shen Senglong and Sengzhao for administrative skill—Gaozu took both in.
translations.idiomatic: Yu recommended his clansmen Shen Senglong and Sengzhao for administrative skill—Gaozu took both in.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職，起爲振武將軍、餘姚令。

translations.literal: He left office on mother's mourning, then was recalled as General Who Quells Martial Affairs and Magistrate of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on mother's mourning, then was recalled as General Who Quells Martial Affairs and magistrate of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 縣大姓虞氏千餘家，請謁如市，前後令長莫能絕。

translations.literal: In the county the great Yu clan numbered over a thousand households—entreaties crowded like a market; successive magistrates could never stop it.
translations.idiomatic: In the county the great Yu clan numbered over a thousand households—entreaties crowded like a market; successive magistrates could never stop it.

sentences.zh: 自瑀到，非訟所通，其有至者，悉立之階下，以法繩之。

translations.literal: From Yu's arrival, what did not belong to litigation—if any came, he had them all stand below the steps and bound them with law.
translations.idiomatic: From Yu's arrival, what did not belong to litigation—if any came, he had them all stand below the steps and bound them with law.

sentences.zh: 縣南又有豪族數百家，子弟縱橫，遞相庇廕，厚自封植，百姓甚患之。

translations.literal: South of the county were also several hundred powerful clans; their sons and younger kin ran wild, shielding one another in turn, thickly planting themselves—common folk greatly suffered.
translations.idiomatic: South of the county were also several hundred powerful clans; their sons and younger kin ran wild, shielding one another and thickly planting themselves—common folk greatly suffered.

sentences.zh: 瑀召其老者爲石頭倉監，少者補縣僮，皆號泣道路，自是權右屏跡。

translations.literal: Yu summoned their elders as overseers of the Stone Fort granary, the younger as county runners—all wailed on the roads; from then the mighty hid their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Yu summoned their elders as overseers of the Stone Fort granary, the younger as county runners—all wailed on the roads; from then the mighty hid their tracks.

sentences.zh: 瑀初至，富吏皆鮮衣美服，以自彰別。

translations.literal: When Yu first arrived, rich clerks all wore bright clothes and fine dress to distinguish themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu first arrived, rich clerks all wore bright clothes and fine dress to distinguish themselves.

sentences.zh: 瑀怒曰：「汝等下縣吏，何自擬貴人耶？

translations.literal: Yu angrily said: "You are low county clerks—why do you compare yourselves to the nobly born?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu angrily said, "You are low county clerks—why do you compare yourselves to the nobly born?"

sentences.zh: 」悉使著芒屩粗布，侍立終日，足有蹉跌，輒加榜棰。

translations.literal: " He had them all wear straw sandals and coarse cloth, standing attendance all day—if the feet stumbled he added the rod.
translations.idiomatic: " he had them all wear straw sandals and coarse cloth, standing attendance all day—if the feet stumbled he added the rod.

sentences.zh: 瑀微時，嘗自至此鬻瓦器，爲富人所辱，故因以報焉，由是士庶駭怨。

translations.literal: When Yu was still obscure he had once come here selling pottery and was humiliated by a rich man—therefore he took this chance to repay; hence gentlemen and commoners were alarmed and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu was still obscure he had once come here selling pottery and was humiliated by a rich man—therefore he took this chance to repay; hence gentlemen and commoners were alarmed and resentful.

sentences.zh: 然瑀廉白自守，故得遂行其志。

translations.literal: Yet Yu kept himself pure and white, and so could carry out his will.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yu kept himself pure and white, and so could carry out his will.

sentences.zh: 後王師北伐，徵瑀爲建威將軍，督運漕，尋兼都水使者。

translations.literal: Later when the royal army marched north, Yu was summoned as General Who Establishes Might, supervising transport; soon he was additionally Commissioner of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Later when the royal army marched north, Yu was summoned as General Who Establishes Might, supervising transport; soon he was additionally Commissioner of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷少府卿。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Minister of the Palace Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Minister of the Palace Supplies.

sentences.zh: 出爲安南長史、尋陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk of the Army of the South and Administrator of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as chief clerk of the Army of the South and administrator of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史曹景宗疾篤，瑀行府州事。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiangzhou Cao Jingzong was gravely ill—Yu acted for the prefecture and province.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Jiangzhou Cao Jingzong was gravely ill—Yu acted for the prefecture and province.

sentences.zh: 景宗卒，仍爲信威蕭穎達長史，太守如故。

translations.literal: When Jingzong died, he became Chief Clerk to Xiao Yingda of Trustworthy Might, administrator as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong died, he became chief clerk to Xiao Yingda of Trustworthy Might, administrator as before.

sentences.zh: 瑀性屈強，每忤穎達，穎達銜之。

translations.literal: Yu by nature was stubborn and unyielding—often opposing Yingda; Yingda bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Yu by nature was stubborn and unyielding—often opposing Yingda; Yingda bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 天監八年，因入諮事，辭又激厲，穎達作色曰：「朝廷用君作行事耶？

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianjian, when entering to consult on affairs, his words were again fierce—Yingda showed anger: "Did the court employ you as a mere acting officer?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianjian, when entering to consult on affairs, his words were again fierce—Yingda showed anger, "Did the court employ you as a mere acting officer?"

sentences.zh: 」瑀出，謂人曰：「我死而後已，終不能傾側面從。

translations.literal: " Yu left and told others: "Only after I die will I stop—I can never lean and turn my face to follow.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu left and told others, "Only after I die will I stop—I can never lean and turn my face to follow.

sentences.zh: 」是日，于路爲盜所殺，時年五十九，多以爲穎達害焉。

translations.literal: " That same day on the road he was killed by bandits—aged fifty-nine; many believed Yingda had harmed him.
translations.idiomatic: " that same day on the road he was killed by bandits—aged fifty-nine; many believed Yingda had harmed him.

sentences.zh: 子續累訟之，遇穎達亦尋卒，事遂不窮竟。

translations.literal: His son Xu repeatedly sued; Yingda also soon died—the matter was never fully pursued.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu repeatedly sued; Yingda also soon died—the matter was never fully pursued.

sentences.zh: 續乃布衣蔬食終其身。

translations.literal: Xu thereafter wore hemp and ate vegetables to the end of his days.
translations.idiomatic: Xu thereafter wore hemp and ate vegetables to the end of his days.

sentences.zh: 范述曾

translations.literal: Fan Shuzeng
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shuzeng

sentences.zh: 范述曾字子玄，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Fan Shuzeng, styled Zixuan, was a man of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shuzeng, styled Zixuan, came from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼好學，從餘杭呂道惠受《五經》，略通章句。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning; from Yuhang's Lü Daohui he received the Five Classics and broadly grasped their clause-and-commentary.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved learning; from Yuhang's Lü Daohui he received the Five Classics and broadly grasped their clause-and-commentary.

sentences.zh: 道惠學徒常有百數，獨稱述曾曰：「此子必爲王者師。

translations.literal: Daohui's students often numbered a hundred, yet he alone praised Shuzeng: "This boy will surely be teacher to a king.
translations.idiomatic: Daohui's students often numbered a hundred, yet he alone praised Shuzeng, "This boy will surely be teacher to a king.

sentences.zh: 」齊文惠太子、竟陵文宣王幼時，高帝引述曾爲之師友。

translations.literal: " In Qi, when the Filial and Cultured Heir and Prince of Jingling the Cultured and Sagely were young, Emperor Gao brought in Shuzeng as their teacher and friend.
translations.idiomatic: " in Qi, when the Filial and Cultured Heir and Prince of Jingling the Cultured and Sagely were young, Emperor Gao brought in Shuzeng as their teacher and friend.

sentences.zh: 起家爲宋晉熙王國侍郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as Gentleman of the Kingdom of Prince Jinxi of Song.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Gentleman of the Kingdom of Prince Jinxi of Song.

sentences.zh: 齊初，至南郡王國郎中令，遷尚書主客郎、太子步兵校尉，帶開陽令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi he reached Commandant of the Kingdom of the Prince of Nankeng, then was transferred to Master of Guests in the Secretariat, Colonel of Footsoldiers of the Heir Apparent, and concurrently Magistrate of Kaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qi he reached Commandant of the Kingdom of the Prince of Nankeng, then was transferred to Master of Guests in the Secretariat, Colonel of Footsoldiers of the Heir Apparent, and concurrently magistrate of Kaiyang.

sentences.zh: 述曾爲人謇諤，在宮多所諫爭，太子雖不能全用，然亦弗之罪也。

translations.literal: Shuzeng as a man was blunt and upright; in the palace he often remonstrated—the Heir Apparent could not fully employ his counsel, yet did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzeng as a man was blunt and upright; in the palace he often remonstrated—the Heir Apparent could not fully employ his counsel, yet did not blame him.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王深相器重，號爲「周舍」。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingling valued him deeply and called him "Zhou She."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jingling valued him deeply and called him "Zhou She."

sentences.zh: 時太子左衛率沈約亦以述曾方汲黯。

translations.literal: At the time Left Guard Commandant of the Heir Apparent Shen Yue also compared Shuzeng to Ji An.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Left Guard Commandant of the Heir Apparent Shen Yue also compared Shuzeng to Ji An.

sentences.zh: 以父母年老，乞還就養，乃拜中散大夫。

translations.literal: Because his parents were old, he begged to return and support them—he was appointed Grand Master with Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Because his parents were old, he begged to return and support them—he was appointed Grand Master with Leisure.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，除遊擊將軍，出爲永嘉太守。

translations.literal: When Mingdi took the throne he was made General Who Patrols and Attacks and went out as Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingdi took the throne he was made General Who Patrols and Attacks and went out as administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 爲政清平，不尚威猛，民俗便之。

translations.literal: In governance he was clear and level, not favoring fierceness—the folk found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In governance he was clear and level, not favoring fierceness—the folk found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 所部橫陽縣，山谷險峻，爲逋逃所聚，前後二千石討捕莫能息。

translations.literal: Within his jurisdiction Hengyang County had steep mountain valleys where fugitives gathered—successive two-thousand-bushel officials hunted them without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Within his jurisdiction Hengyang County had steep mountain valleys where fugitives gathered—successive two-thousand-bushel officials hunted them without cease.

sentences.zh: 述曾下車，開示恩信，凡諸凶黨，繦負而出，編戶屬籍者二百餘家。

translations.literal: When Shuzeng took office he opened with grace and trust—all violent factions came out carrying infants on their backs; over two hundred households were registered and enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuzeng took office he opened with grace and trust—all violent factions came out carrying infants on their backs; over two hundred households were registered and enrolled.

sentences.zh: 自是商賈流通，居民安業。

translations.literal: From then merchants flowed and residents rested in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: From then merchants flowed and residents rested in their occupations.

sentences.zh: 在郡勵志清白，不受饋遺，明帝聞甚嘉之，下詔褒美焉。

translations.literal: In the commandery he urged his will toward purity and whiteness, accepted no gifts or presents, Emperor Ming heard and greatly praised him, and issued an edict commending him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he kept to pure conduct and refused gifts; Emperor Ming heard of it, greatly approved, and issued an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 徵爲遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as General Who Attacks with Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as General Who Attacks with Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 郡送故舊錢二十餘萬，述曾一無所受。

translations.literal: The commandery sent more than two hundred thousand cash from old acquaintances, and Shuzeng accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery sent over two hundred thousand cash from old associates; Shuzeng refused it all.

sentences.zh: 始之郡，不將家屬；

translations.literal: When he first went to the commandery, he did not bring his family;
translations.idiomatic: When he first took office, he came without his family;

sentences.zh: 及還，吏無荷擔者。

translations.literal: when he returned, no clerk bore burdens.
translations.idiomatic: when he returned, no clerk carried a load.

sentences.zh: 民無老少，皆出拜辭，號哭聞于數十里。

translations.literal: Young and old among the people all came out to bow and bid farewell, and their wailing could be heard for dozens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Young and old came out to bow farewell; their wailing was heard for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 東昏時，拜中散大夫，還鄉里。

translations.literal: At the time of Dong Hun, he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Leisure and returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dong Hun he became Grand Master of Palace Leisure and returned home.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，乃輕舟出詣闕，仍辭還東。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, he then took a light boat to go to the palace gate, yet declined and returned east.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he came by light boat to court, then declined and returned east.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔曰：「中散大夫范述曾，昔在齊世，忠直奉主，往蒞永嘉，治身廉約，宜加禮秩，以厲清操。

translations.literal: Gaozu's edict said: "Grand Master of Palace Leisure Fan Shuzeng—in Qi times was loyal and upright in serving his lord; when he went to govern Yongjia he governed his person with frugality and restraint. He should receive increased rank and salary to encourage pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's edict said: "Grand Master of Palace Leisure Fan Shuzeng served his lord loyally in Qi; governing Yongjia he lived in frugal integrity. Increase his rank and salary to encourage pure conduct.

sentences.zh: 可太中大夫，賜絹二十匹。」

translations.literal: Let him be Grand Master of Palace Leisure with Regular Attendance, and award twenty bolts of silk."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint him Grand Master of Palace Leisure with Regular Attendance and award twenty bolts of silk."

sentences.zh: 述曾生平得奉祿，皆以分施。

translations.literal: Throughout his life Shuzeng received salary and always divided it to bestow upon others.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzeng's salary he always divided and gave away.

sentences.zh: 及老，遂壁立無所資。

translations.literal: When old, he stood like a wall with nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he had nothing to his name.

sentences.zh: 以天監八年卒，時年七十九。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianjian he died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianjian he died, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 注《易文言》，著雜詩賦數十篇。

translations.literal: He annotated the Changes "Words on Language" and authored several tens of chapters of miscellaneous poetry and fu.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the Changes "Words on Language" and wrote several tens of chapters of miscellaneous poetry and fu.

sentences.zh: 丘仲孚

translations.literal: Qiu Zhongfu
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Zhongfu

sentences.zh: 丘仲孚字公信，吳興烏程人也。

translations.literal: Qiu Zhongfu, courtesy name Gongxin, was a man of Wucheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Zhongfu, styled Gongxin, came from Wucheng in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 少好學，從祖靈鞠有人倫之鑒，常稱爲千里駒也。

translations.literal: As a youth he loved learning; his father's cousin Lingju had a discerning eye for men and often called him a colt of a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved learning; his cousin Lingju had a discerning eye for men and often called him a colt of a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 齊永明初，選爲國子生，舉高第，未調，還鄉里。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming in Qi, he was selected as a National University student, achieved highest rank, but before appointment returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongming in Qi he was selected as a National University student, ranked highest, but before appointment returned home.

sentences.zh: 家貧，無以自資，乃結羣盜，爲之計畫，劫掠三吳。

translations.literal: His family was poor and could not support themselves, so he joined a band of robbers, planning for them and raiding the Three Wu regions.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and could not support themselves, so he joined a band of robbers, planned their raids, and plundered the Three Wu.

sentences.zh: 仲孚聰明有智略，羣盜畏而服之，所行皆果，故亦不發。

translations.literal: Zhongfu was clever and resourceful; the band feared and obeyed him, and their actions all succeeded, so they were never exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and resourceful, Zhongfu made the band fear and obey him; their raids always succeeded and they were never caught.

sentences.zh: 太守徐嗣召補主簿，歷揚州從事、太學博士、于湖令，有能名。

translations.literal: Prefect Xu Si summoned him to fill the post of chief clerk; he served as Yangzhou staff officer, National University erudite, and magistrate of Yuhu, gaining a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Xu Si made him chief clerk; he served as Yangzhou staff officer, National University erudite, and magistrate of Yuhu, gaining a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 太守呂文顯當時倖臣，陵詆屬縣，仲孚獨不爲之屈。

translations.literal: Prefect Lü Wenxian was a favored minister of the time and insulted subordinate counties; only Zhongfu would not yield to him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Lü Wenxian, a court favorite, bullied subordinate counties; only Zhongfu would not yield.

sentences.zh: 以父喪去職。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on his father's death.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，起爲烈武將軍、曲阿令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he was recalled as General of Fierce Martiality and magistrate of Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he was recalled as General of Fierce Martiality and magistrate of Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 值會稽太守王敬則舉兵反，乘朝廷不備，反問始至，而前鋒已屆曲阿。

translations.literal: It happened that the Administrator of Kuaiji, Wang Jingze, raised troops in rebellion; taking advantage of the court's unpreparedness, word of the revolt had just arrived when the vanguard already reached Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji Administrator Wang Jingze raised troops in rebellion; catching the court unprepared, word had just arrived when the vanguard already reached Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 仲孚謂吏民曰：「賊乘勝雖銳，而烏合易離。

translations.literal: Zhongfu told clerks and people: "Though the rebels are sharp riding victory, a mob easily gathered will easily scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu told clerks and people: "Though the rebels are sharp on victory, a mob easily gathered will easily scatter.

sentences.zh: 今若收船艦，鑿長崗埭，泄瀆水以阻其路，得留數日，臺軍必至，則大事濟矣。

translations.literal: If we now gather boats and ships, cut the Changgang dam, release the sluice waters to block their path, and can hold for several days, the metropolitan army will surely arrive—then the great affair will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Gather boats, cut the Changgang dam, release the sluice waters to block their path, and hold for several days—the metropolitan army will arrive and the great affair will succeed."

sentences.zh: 」敬則軍至，值瀆涸，果頓兵不得進，遂敗散。

translations.literal: When Jingze's army arrived, the sluice had run dry and he indeed halted his troops and could not advance, and so was defeated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingze's army arrived, the sluice had run dry; he halted and could not advance, and was defeated and scattered.

sentences.zh: 仲孚以距守有功，遷山陰令，居職甚有聲稱，百姓爲之謠曰：「二傅沈劉，不如一丘。

translations.literal: Zhongfu for meritorious defense was transferred to magistrate of Shanyin; in office he had great renown, and the people made a song: "Two Fus, Shen, and Liu—none equals one Qiu."
translations.idiomatic: For meritorious defense Zhongfu was transferred to magistrate of Shanyin; in office he won great renown, and the people sang: "Two Fus, Shen, and Liu—none equals one Qiu."

sentences.zh: 」前世傅琰父子、沈憲、劉玄明，相繼宰山陰，並有政績，言仲孚皆過之也。

translations.literal: In earlier generations Fu Yan and his son, Shen Xian, and Liu Xuanming had successively governed Shanyin, all with political achievements—the saying meant Zhongfu surpassed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Fu Yan and his son, Shen Xian, and Liu Xuanming had successively governed Shanyin with distinction—the saying meant Zhongfu surpassed them all.

sentences.zh: 齊末政亂，頗有贓賄，爲有司所舉，將收之，仲孚竊逃，徑還京師詣闕，會赦，得不治。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi, government was chaotic and there was much bribery; reported by the authorities and about to be arrested, Zhongfu secretly fled, went straight back to the capital to present himself at court, and met an amnesty—thus escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qi, government was chaotic and bribery rife; reported and about to be arrested, Zhongfu secretly fled to the capital and presented himself at court; an amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，復爲山陰令。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, he again became magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he again became magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 仲孚長於撥煩，善適權變，吏民敬服，號稱神明，治爲天下第一。

translations.literal: Zhongfu excelled at cutting through tangles and was adept at adapting to circumstances; clerks and people respected and obeyed him, called him divine in governance, and his administration was ranked first under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu excelled at cutting through red tape and adapting to circumstances; clerks and people revered him, called him divine, and his administration ranked first under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 超遷車騎長史、長沙內史，視事未朞，徵爲尚書右丞，遷左丞，仍擢爲衛尉卿，恩任甚厚。

translations.literal: He was exceptionally promoted to Chief Clerk of the Chariots and Cavalry and Internal Administrator of Changsha; before his term ended he was summoned as Right Director of the Masters of Writing, transferred to Left Director, then promoted to Minister of the Guard—all with great favor and trust.
translations.idiomatic: He was exceptionally promoted to Chief Clerk of the Chariots and Cavalry and internal administrator of Changsha; before his term ended he became Right Director of the Masters of Writing, then Left Director, then Minister of the Guard—with great favor.

sentences.zh: 初起雙闕，以仲孚領大匠。

translations.literal: When the Twin Gate-towers were first built, Zhongfu was put in charge as Master of Crafts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Twin Gate-towers were first built, Zhongfu served as Master of Crafts.

sentences.zh: 事畢，出爲安西長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: When the work was done, he went out as Chief Clerk of the Pacifying West and Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done, he went out as Chief Clerk of the Pacifying West and administrator of Nan.

sentences.zh: 遷雲麾長史、江夏太守，行郢州州府事，遭母憂，起攝職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Cloudy Banner and Administrator of Jiangxia, acting on Yingzhou prefectural affairs; he encountered mourning for his mother but was recalled to hold office provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Chief Clerk of the Cloudy Banner and administrator of Jiangxia, acting on Yingzhou affairs; he mourned his mother but was recalled to hold office.

sentences.zh: 坐事除名，復起爲司空參軍。

translations.literal: For an offense he was dismissed from the register; later he was recalled as staff officer to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was dismissed; later recalled as staff officer to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 俄遷豫章內史，在郡更勵清節。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Internal Administrator of Yuzhang; in the commandery he further urged pure integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he became internal administrator of Yuzhang and further urged pure integrity in office.

sentences.zh: 頃之，卒，時年四十八。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, aged forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「豫章內史丘仲孚，重試大邦，責以後效，非直悔吝云亡，實亦政績克舉。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Internal Administrator Qiu Zhongfu of Yuzhang was tried again in a great commandery and charged with later results—not merely regret that is gone, but in truth his political achievements were fully attained.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Internal Administrator Qiu Zhongfu of Yuzhang was tried in a great commandery and charged with later results—not merely regret at his loss, but his achievements were fully attained.

sentences.zh: 不幸殞喪，良以傷惻。

translations.literal: His untimely death is truly heart-wrenching.
translations.idiomatic: His untimely death is truly heart-wrenching.

sentences.zh: 可贈給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Let him posthumously receive Attendant of Affairs and Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate."
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously award him Attendant of Affairs and Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate."

sentences.zh: 」仲孚喪將還，豫章老幼號哭攀送，車輪不得前。

translations.literal: As Zhongfu's coffin was about to return, old and young of Yuzhang wailed and clung to see him off—the carriage wheels could not move forward.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhongfu's coffin was about to return, old and young of Yuzhang wailed and clung to see him off—the wheels could not turn.

sentences.zh: 仲孚爲左丞，撰《皇典》二十卷、《南宮故事》百卷，又撰《尚書具事雜儀》，行於世焉。

translations.literal: When Zhongfu was Left Director, he compiled twenty chapters of the Imperial Canon and one hundred chapters of Southern Palace Precedents, and also compiled Miscellaneous Rituals of the Masters of Writing with Complete Particulars, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: As Left Director, Zhongfu compiled twenty chapters of the Imperial Canon and one hundred of Southern Palace Precedents, plus Miscellaneous Rituals of the Masters of Writing with Complete Particulars—all circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 孫謙字長遜，東莞莒人也。

translations.literal: Sun Qian, courtesy name Changxun, was a man of Ju in Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qian, styled Changxun, came from Ju in Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 少爲親人趙伯符所知。

translations.literal: As a youth he was recognized by his kinsman Zhao Bofu.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was recognized by his kinsman Zhao Bofu.

sentences.zh: 謙年十七，伯符爲豫州刺史，引爲左軍行參軍，以治幹稱。

translations.literal: When Qian was seventeen, Bofu was Inspector of Yuzhou and brought him in as Acting Military Staff Officer of the Left Army, renowned for governing competence.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, when Bofu was inspector of Yuzhou, he brought Qian in as acting military staff officer of the Left Army, renowned for governing competence.

sentences.zh: 父憂去職，客居歷陽，躬耕以養弟妹，鄉里稱其敦睦。

translations.literal: He left office on his father's death, lived as a guest in Liyang, personally tilled fields to support younger siblings, and the village praised his warm harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on his father's death, lived in Liyang, tilled fields to support younger siblings, and the village praised his warm harmony.

sentences.zh: 宋江夏王義恭聞之，引爲行參軍，歷仕大司馬、太宰二府。

translations.literal: In Song, Prince Jiangxia Wang Yigong heard of it and brought him in as acting staff officer; he served through both the Grand Marshal's and Grand Tutor's offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Song, Prince Jiangxia Wang Yigong heard of it and brought him in as acting staff officer; he served in both the Grand Marshal's and Grand Tutor's offices.

sentences.zh: 出爲句容令，清慎強記，縣人號爲神明。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Gou Rong, pure, cautious, and with strong memory—the county people called him divine.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as magistrate of Gou Rong—pure, cautious, with strong memory—and the county people called him divine.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，事建安王休仁，休仁以爲司徒參軍，言之明帝，擢爲明威將軍、巴東、建平二郡太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he served Prince Jian'an Wang Xiuren; Xiuren made him staff officer to the Minister of Education and spoke of him to Emperor Ming, who promoted him to General of Illustrious Might and Administrator of the two commanderies of Badong and Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taishi he served Prince Jian'an Wang Xiuren, who made him staff officer to the Minister of Education and recommended him to Emperor Ming, who promoted him to General of Illustrious Might and administrator of Badong and Jianping.

sentences.zh: 郡居三峽，恒以威力鎮之。

translations.literal: The commandery lay in the Three Gorges; constantly they used armed might to control it.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery lay in the Three Gorges and was constantly controlled by armed might.

sentences.zh: 謙將述職，敕募千人自隨。

translations.literal: When Qian was about to report to his post, an edict ordered recruiting a thousand men to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian was about to take office, an edict ordered a thousand men recruited to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 謙曰：「蠻夷不賓，蓋待之失節耳。

translations.literal: Qian said: "The barbarians do not submit—surely it is because they are treated without proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: Qian said: "The barbarians do not submit because they are treated without proper measure.

sentences.zh: 何煩兵役，以爲國費。

translations.literal: Why trouble military service and burden state expense?"
translations.idiomatic: Why trouble military service and burden state expense?"

sentences.zh: 」固辭不受。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 至郡，布恩惠之化，蠻獠懷之，競餉金寶，謙慰喻而遣，一無所納。

translations.literal: Reaching the commandery he spread benevolent transforming influence; the Man and Liao cherished him and competed to offer gold and jewels—Qian comforted and instructed them and sent them away, accepting none.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the commandery he spread benevolent rule; the Man and Liao cherished him and competed to offer gold and jewels—Qian comforted them and sent them away, accepting none.

sentences.zh: 及掠得生口，皆放還家。

translations.literal: When captives were taken in raids, he released them all to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Captives taken in raids he released to return home.

sentences.zh: 俸秩出吏民者，悉原除之。

translations.literal: Salary levies drawn from clerks and people—he remitted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Salary levies drawn from clerks and people he remitted entirely.

sentences.zh: 郡境翕然，威信大著。

translations.literal: The commandery realm settled in harmony; prestige and trust greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery settled in harmony; prestige and trust greatly flourished.

sentences.zh: 視事三年，徵還爲撫軍中兵參軍。

translations.literal: After three years in office he was summoned back as Military Staff Officer of the Pacification Army Central Regiment.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he was summoned back as military staff officer of the Pacification Army Central Regiment.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，遷梁州刺史，辭不赴職，遷越騎校尉、征北司馬府主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui he was transferred to Inspector of Liangzhou, declined and did not take office, and was transferred to Colonel of Rapid Cavalry and chief clerk of the Northern Expedition Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanhui he was transferred to inspector of Liangzhou but declined; he was then made Colonel of Rapid Cavalry and chief clerk of the Northern Expedition Grand Marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 建平王將稱兵，患謙強直，託事遣使京師，然後作亂。

translations.literal: Prince Jianping was about to raise troops and feared Qian's stern uprightness; he contrived an affair to send him as envoy to the capital, then launched rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jianping planned to raise troops and feared Qian's stern uprightness; he contrived an affair to send him as envoy to the capital, then rebelled.

sentences.zh: 及建平誅，遷左軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Jianping was executed, he was transferred to General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianping was executed, he was transferred to General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 天監六年，出爲輔國將軍、零陵太守，已衰老，猶強力爲政，吏民安之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianjian he went out as General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Lingling; though already aged, he still governed with force—clerks and people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianjian he went out as General Who Assists the State and administrator of Lingling; though aged, he still governed vigorously—clerks and people were at peace.

sentences.zh: 先是，郡多虎暴，謙至絕迹。

translations.literal: Before this the commandery had many violent tigers; when Qian arrived they vanished utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Before this the commandery had many violent tigers; when Qian arrived they vanished.

sentences.zh: 及去官之夜，虎卽害居民。

translations.literal: On the night he left office, a tiger at once harmed residents.
translations.idiomatic: The night he left office, a tiger at once harmed residents.

sentences.zh: 謙爲郡縣，常勤勸課農桑，務盡地利，收入常多於鄰境。

translations.literal: When Qian served commanderies and counties he always diligently urged farming and sericulture, striving to use all land to advantage—revenue constantly exceeded neighboring regions.
translations.idiomatic: Serving commanderies and counties he always urged farming and sericulture and strove to use all land—revenue constantly exceeded neighboring regions.

sentences.zh: 九年，以年老，徵爲光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, because of age, he was summoned as Grand Master of Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, because of age, he was summoned as Grand Master of Splendor.

sentences.zh: 旣至，高祖嘉其清潔，甚禮異焉。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Gaozu praised his purity and treated him with great special honor.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Gaozu praised his purity and treated him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 每朝見，猶請劇職自效。

translations.literal: At every court audience he still requested heavy duties to prove himself.
translations.idiomatic: At every court audience he still requested heavy duties to prove himself.

sentences.zh: 高祖笑曰：「朕使卿智，不使卿力。

translations.literal: Gaozu laughed and said: "I employ your wisdom, not your strength."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed and said: "I employ your wisdom, not your strength."

sentences.zh: 」十四年，詔曰：「光祿大夫孫謙，清慎有聞，白首不怠，高年舊齒，宜加優秩。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, an edict said: "Grand Master of Splendor Sun Qian—pure and cautious with fame, white-haired yet unwearying, old in years and elder in rank—should receive preferential rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, an edict said: "Grand Master of Splendor Sun Qian—pure and cautious, white-haired yet unwearying, old in years and rank—deserves preferential rank.

sentences.zh: 可給親信二十人，幷給扶。」

translations.literal: Let him be granted twenty trusted attendants, together with a walking staff."
translations.idiomatic: Grant him twenty trusted attendants and a walking staff."

sentences.zh: 謙自少及老，歷二縣五郡，所在廉潔。

translations.literal: From youth to old age, Qian served two counties and five commanderies—in every place, incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age Qian served two counties and five commanderies—incorrupt in every place.

sentences.zh: 居身儉素，床施蘧蒢屏風，冬則布被莞席，夏日無幬帳，而夜臥未嘗有蚊蚋，人多異焉。

translations.literal: His person was frugal and plain: his bed had screens of arrowroot and coarse rush; in winter, cotton quilts and cattail mats; in summer no mosquito curtains—yet sleeping at night he never had mosquitoes or gnats, and many found this strange.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and plain in person: his bed had arrowroot and coarse-rush screens; in winter cotton quilts and cattail mats; in summer no mosquito curtains—yet he never had mosquitoes or gnats at night, and many found this strange.

sentences.zh: 年逾九十，強壯如五十者，每朝會，輒先衆到公門。

translations.literal: Past ninety years, strong as a man of fifty—at every court assembly he always arrived at the gate before the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Past ninety, strong as a man of fifty—at every court assembly he always arrived at the gate before the crowd.

sentences.zh: 力於仁義，行己過人甚遠。

translations.literal: He exerted himself in benevolence and righteousness; his personal conduct far exceeded others.
translations.idiomatic: He exerted himself in benevolence and righteousness; his conduct far exceeded others.

sentences.zh: 從兄靈慶常病寄于謙，謙出行還問起居。

translations.literal: His older male cousin Lingqing was often ill and lodged with Qian; when Qian went out and returned he would ask after his health.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Lingqing was often ill and lodged with Qian; when Qian went out and returned he asked after his health.

sentences.zh: 靈慶曰：「向飲冷熱不調，卽時猶渴。

translations.literal: Lingqing said: "Just now I drank something hot and cold out of balance—still thirsty at once."
translations.idiomatic: Lingqing said: "Just now I drank something hot and cold out of balance—I am still thirsty."

sentences.zh: 」謙退遣其妻。

translations.literal: Qian withdrew and sent his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Qian withdrew and sent his wife.

sentences.zh: 有彭城劉融者，行乞疾篤無所歸，友人輿送謙舍，謙開廳事以待之。

translations.literal: There was a Pengcheng man Liu Rong, a wandering beggar desperately ill with nowhere to go; a friend carried him in a litter to Qian's house, and Qian opened the reception hall to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rong of Pengcheng was a wandering beggar, desperately ill with nowhere to go; a friend carried him to Qian's house, and Qian opened the reception hall to await him.

sentences.zh: 及融死，以禮殯葬之。

translations.literal: When Rong died, he buried him with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died, he buried him with full rites.

sentences.zh: 衆咸服其行義。

translations.literal: All admired his righteous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: All admired his righteous conduct.

sentences.zh: 十五年，卒官，時年九十二。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died in office, aged ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he died in office, aged ninety-two.

sentences.zh: 詔賻錢三萬、布五十匹。

translations.literal: An edict awarded funeral gifts of thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: An edict awarded funeral gifts of thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 高祖爲舉哀，甚悼惜之。

translations.literal: Gaozu held mourning for him and deeply lamented his loss.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu held mourning for him and deeply lamented his loss.

sentences.zh: 謙從子廉，便辟巧宦。

translations.literal: Qian's nephew by the younger male line, Lian, was smooth and clever in office-seeking.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's nephew Lian was smooth and clever in office-seeking.

sentences.zh: 齊時已歷大縣，尚書右丞。

translations.literal: In Qi times he had already served large counties and been Right Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi he had already served large counties and been Right Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 天監初，沈約、范雲當朝用事，廉傾意奉之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, Shen Yue and Fan Yun held power in court; Lian inclined his will to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianjian, Shen Yue and Fan Yun held power; Lian inclined himself to serve them.

sentences.zh: 及中書舍人黃睦之等，亦尤所結附。

translations.literal: With Palace Secretariat Attendants Huang Muzhi and others he was especially connected and attached.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially connected with Palace Secretariat Attendants Huang Muzhi and others.

sentences.zh: 凡貴要每食，廉必日進滋旨，皆手自煎調，不辭勤劇，遂得爲列卿、御史中丞、晉陵、吳興太守。

translations.literal: Whenever the noble and powerful dined, Lian would daily send rich delicacies, all personally fried and seasoned, not shunning toil—thus attaining rank among ministers, Censor-in-Chief, and Administrator of Jinling and Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the noble and powerful dined, Lian daily sent rich delicacies, all personally prepared, not shunning toil—thus attaining ministerial rank, Censor-in-Chief, and administrator of Jinling and Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 時廣陵高爽有險薄才，客於廉，廉委以文記，爽嘗有求不稱意，乃爲屐謎以喻廉曰：「刺鼻不知嚏，蹋面不知瞋，齧齒作步數，持此得勝人。

translations.literal: At the time Gaoling's Gao Shuang had a sharp and shallow talent; lodging with Lian, Lian entrusted him with documents; Shuang once had a request unmet and made a riddle on clogs to mock Lian: "Pierced nose knows not to sneeze, stepped face knows not to rage, gnashing teeth count paces—with this one outdoes men."
translations.idiomatic: Gaoling's Gao Shuang had a sharp, shallow talent; lodging with Lian, Lian entrusted him with documents; once denied a request, Shuang made a clog riddle to mock Lian: "Pierced nose knows not to sneeze, stepped face knows not to rage, gnashing teeth count paces—with this one outdoes men."

sentences.zh: 」譏其不計恥辱，以此取名位也。

translations.literal: It mocked him for not counting disgrace and thus winning name and rank.
translations.idiomatic: It mocked him for ignoring disgrace to win name and rank.

sentences.zh: 伏暅字玄耀，曼容之子也。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan, courtesy name Xuanyao, was Manrong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan, styled Xuanyao, was Manrong's son.

sentences.zh: 幼傳父業，能言玄理，與樂安任昉、彭城劉曼俱知名。

translations.literal: As a child he inherited his father's learning, could discourse on abstruse principles, and was renowned together with Ren Fang of Le'an and Liu Man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he inherited his father's learning, could discourse on abstruse principles, and was renowned with Ren Fang of Le'an and Liu Man of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 起家齊奉朝請，仍兼太學博士，尋除東陽郡丞，秩滿爲鄞令。

translations.literal: He began as Qi Court Gentleman for the Dynasty, concurrently National University erudite; soon removed as Assistant Administrator of Dongyang commandery, and at term's end became magistrate of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Qi Court Gentleman for the Dynasty, concurrently National University erudite; soon became assistant administrator of Dongyang, and at term's end became magistrate of Yin.

sentences.zh: 時曼容已致仕，故頻以外職處暅，令其得養焉。

translations.literal: At the time Manrong had already retired, so repeatedly he was placed in outer posts so Xuan could support him.
translations.idiomatic: Manrong had already retired, so Xuan was repeatedly placed in outer posts so he could support him.

sentences.zh: 齊末，始爲尚書都官郎，仍爲衛軍記室參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi he first became Director in the Ministry of Justice Section of the Masters of Writing, then Staff Secretary in the Guard Army office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qi he first became Director in the Ministry of Justice Section, then staff secretary in the Guard Army office.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，遷國子博士，父憂去職。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, he was transferred to Erudite of the National University; on his father's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he was made Erudite of the National University, then left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，爲車騎諮議參軍，累遷司空長史、中書侍郎、前軍將軍、兼《五經》博士，與吏部尚書徐勉、中書侍郎周捨，總知五禮事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became Army Adviser on the Chariots and Cavalry Campaign, rising through Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works, Attendant of the Secretariat, General of the Vanguard, and concurrent Erudite of the Five Classics; with Minister of Personnel Xu Mian and Attendant of the Secretariat Zhou She he oversaw the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he served as Army Adviser on the Chariots and Cavalry Campaign, then rose through Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works, Attendant of the Secretariat, General of the Vanguard, and concurrent Erudite of the Five Classics; with Xu Mian of Personnel and Zhou She of the Secretariat he oversaw the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 出爲永陽內史，在郡清潔，治務安靜。

translations.literal: He went out as Internal Magistrate of Yongyang; in the commandery he was pure and clean, and his governance was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as internal magistrate of Yongyang, governing with purity and quiet efficiency.

sentences.zh: 郡民何貞秀等一百五十四人詣州言狀，湘州刺史以聞。

translations.literal: One hundred fifty-four commandery commoners including He Zhenxiu went to the province to report his conduct; the Inspector of Xiangzhou memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred fifty-four commoners including He Zhenxiu went to the province to praise his conduct, and the inspector of Xiangzhou reported it upward.

sentences.zh: 詔勘有十五事爲吏民所懷，高祖善之，徵爲新安太守。

translations.literal: An edict reviewed and found fifteen matters for which officials and people cherished him; Gaozu approved and summoned him as Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial review found fifteen deeds that officials and people cherished; Gaozu approved and summoned him as administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 在郡清恪，如永陽時。

translations.literal: In the commandery he was pure and scrupulous, as in Yongyang times.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he was pure and scrupulous, as he had been at Yongyang.

sentences.zh: 民賦稅不登者，輒以太守田米助之。

translations.literal: For commoners who could not meet tax levies, he at once supplied them from the administrator's field grain.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners could not meet their tax levies, he paid from the administrator's own field grain.

sentences.zh: 郡多麻苧，家人乃至無以爲繩，其厲志如此。

translations.literal: The commandery had much hemp and ramie, yet his household came to lack even rope for binding—such was his stern resolve.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery abounded in hemp and ramie, yet his household lacked even rope to bind things—such was his austerity.

sentences.zh: 屬縣始新、遂安、海寧，並同時生爲立祠。

translations.literal: The subordinate counties Shixin, Suian, and Haining all while he still lived built shrines to him.
translations.idiomatic: The subordinate counties Shixin, Suian, and Haining all built living shrines to him while he was still in office.

sentences.zh: 徵爲國子博士，領長水校尉。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Erudite of the National University and concurrently Colonel of the Changshui Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Erudite of the National University and concurrently colonel of the Changshui Guard.

sentences.zh: 時始興內史何遠累著清績，高祖詔擢爲黃門侍郎，俄遷信武將軍、監吳郡。

translations.literal: At the time He Yuan, Internal Magistrate of Shixing, had repeatedly shown pure merit; Gaozu edicted his promotion to Attendant of the Yellow Gate, and soon he was transferred to General of Trustworthy Might and Supervisor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the time He Yuan, internal magistrate of Shixing, had repeatedly shown pure merit; Gaozu promoted him to Attendant of the Yellow Gate, and soon made him General of Trustworthy Might and supervisor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 暅自以名輩素在遠前，爲吏俱稱廉白，遠累見擢，暅遷階而已，意望不滿，多托疾居家。

translations.literal: Xuan thought his name and seniority had always ranked above Yuan's—both were called pure in office—yet Yuan was repeatedly promoted while Xuan only advanced in rank; dissatisfied with his prospects, he often pleaded illness and stayed home.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan believed his name and seniority had always outranked Yuan's—both were praised as incorrupt officials—yet Yuan was promoted again and again while Xuan only moved up in rank; bitter and dissatisfied, he often pleaded illness and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 尋求假到東陽迎妹喪，因留會稽築宅，自表解，高祖詔以爲豫章內史，暅乃出拜。

translations.literal: Soon he sought leave to go to Dongyang for his sister's funeral, then stayed in Kuaiji building a house; he memorialized to resign, Gaozu edicted him Internal Magistrate of Yuzhang, and Xuan at last went out to take the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked leave to go to Dongyang for his sister's funeral, then remained in Kuaiji building a house; he memorialized to resign, Gaozu appointed him internal magistrate of Yuzhang, and Xuan at last went out to accept.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史虞㬭奏曰：

translations.literal: Imperial Secretary in the Office of the Censor Yu Yan memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Secretary in the Office of the Censor Yu Yan memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣聞失忠與信，一心之道以虧；

translations.literal: I have heard that when loyalty and trust are lost, the way of single-heartedness is impaired;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when loyalty and trust are lost, the path of undivided devotion is broken;

sentences.zh: 貌是情非，兩觀之誅宜及。

translations.literal: when the face is yes and the heart is no, the execution at the Two Watchtowers should follow.
translations.idiomatic: when appearance and feeling diverge, the punishment of the Two Watchtowers is warranted.

sentences.zh: 未有陵犯名教，要冒君親，而可緯俗經邦者也。

translations.literal: Never has one who violated name and teaching and importuned against lord and kin been fit to weave custom and govern the realm.
translations.idiomatic: No one who tramples name and teaching and importunes lord and kin can weave custom and govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 風聞豫章內史伏暅，去歲啓假，以迎妹喪爲解，因停會稽不去。

translations.literal: By report Internal Magistrate of Yuzhang Fu Xuan, last year sought leave on the pretext of meeting his sister's funeral, then halted in Kuaiji and did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: By report Fu Xuan, internal magistrate of Yuzhang, last year sought leave to meet his sister's funeral, then stayed in Kuaiji and never returned.

sentences.zh: 入東之始，貨宅賣車。

translations.literal: At the start of entering the east, he mortgaged a house and sold a carriage.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he entered the east, he mortgaged a house and sold a carriage.

sentences.zh: 以此而推，則是本無還意。

translations.literal: From this one infers he originally had no intention of returning.
translations.idiomatic: From this one infers he never meant to return.

sentences.zh: 暅歷典二邦，少免貪濁，此自爲政之本，豈得稱功。

translations.literal: Xuan had governed two commanderies and had few taints of greed and corruption—this itself is the root of governing; how can it be called merit?
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had governed two commanderies with little taint of greed— that is merely the baseline of office; how can it be called merit?

sentences.zh: 常謂人才品望，居何遠之右，而遠以清公見擢，名位轉隆，暅深誹怨，形於辭色，興居歎吒，寤寐失圖。

translations.literal: He constantly held that in talent, rank, and reputation he stood above He Yuan, yet Yuan was promoted for pure integrity and name and office rose ever higher; Xuan deeply resented and blamed, showing it in word and face, sighing and lamenting waking and sleeping, losing his design in dreams.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly held that in talent, rank, and reputation he stood above He Yuan, yet Yuan was promoted for pure integrity while name and office rose ever higher; Xuan seethed with resentment, showing it in word and face, sighing day and night and losing sleep over it.

sentences.zh: 天高聽卑，無私不照。

translations.literal: Heaven is high yet listens below; nothing private escapes its light.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is high yet hears what is low; nothing hidden escapes its gaze.

sentences.zh: 去年十二月二十一日詔曰：「國子博士、領長水校尉伏暅，爲政廉平，宜加將養，勿使恚望，致虧士風。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the twelfth month last year an edict said: "Erudite of the National University and Colonel of the Changshui Guard Fu Xuan, governing with pure fairness—nurture him accordingly; do not let resentment and desire impair the scholar's wind.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day of the twelfth month last year an edict said: "Erudite of the National University and colonel of the Changshui Guard Fu Xuan governs with pure fairness; nurture him and do not let resentment impair the scholar's wind.

sentences.zh: 可豫章內史。

translations.literal: Let him be Internal Magistrate of Yuzhang."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be internal magistrate of Yuzhang."

sentences.zh: 」豈有人臣奉如此之詔，而不亡魂破膽，歸罪有司；

translations.literal: Could a minister receiving such an edict fail to lose soul and break gall, returning blame to the responsible office;
translations.idiomatic: Could any minister receiving such an edict fail to lose soul and break gall, turning blame upon himself;

sentences.zh: 擢發抽腸，少自論謝？

translations.literal: pull out hair and rend bowels, and offer some apology?
translations.idiomatic: pull out his hair and rend his bowels in remorse and offer apology?

sentences.zh: 而循奉慠然，了無異色。

translations.literal: Yet he followed and accepted with arrogant composure, showing not the slightest change of color.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he accepted it with arrogant composure, showing not the slightest change of color.

sentences.zh: 暅識見所到，足達此旨，而冒寵不辭，吝斯苟得，故以士流解體，行路沸騰，辯跡求心，無一可恕。

translations.literal: Xuan's insight reaches this far—he fully grasped the intent—yet he accepted favor without declining, stingy in grasping what was opportunely gained; hence scholar-officials dissolved in disgust and travelers seethed; tracing deeds to seek the heart, not one thing can be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan understood this perfectly, yet accepted favor without declining, clinging to opportune gain; scholar-officials were disgusted, travelers seethed, and tracing deed to intent, nothing can be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 竊以暅踉蹡落魄，三十餘年，皇運勃興，咸與維始，除舊佈新，濯之江、漢，一紀之間，三世隆顯。

translations.literal: I venture that Xuan, stumbling and fallen for thirty-odd years, when imperial fortune surged anew—all sharing in the founding, removing the old and spreading the new, washed in the Jiang and Han—in the span of one era three generations rose to glory.
translations.idiomatic: I venture that Xuan, adrift and fallen for thirty-odd years, when imperial fortune surged—all sharing in the founding, washing away the old in the Jiang and Han—in one era three generations rose to glory.

sentences.zh: 曾不能少懷感激，仰答萬分，反覆拙謀，成茲巧罪，不忠不敬，於斯已及。

translations.literal: He could not harbor the least gratitude, repaying the smallest fraction on high; instead by clumsy schemes he wrought this artful crime—disloyalty and disrespect have reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: He could not feel the least gratitude or repay the smallest fraction; instead by clumsy scheming he wrought this artful crime—disloyalty and disrespect have reached this point.

sentences.zh: 請以暅大不敬論。

translations.literal: I ask that Xuan be judged under Great Irreverence.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Xuan be judged under Great Irreverence.

sentences.zh: 以事詳法，應棄市刑，輒收所近獄洗結，以法從事。

translations.literal: Reviewing the matter against the law, he deserves execution and display in market; I have him taken to the nearest prison for examination and closure, to be dealt with by law.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the matter against the law, he deserves execution at market; I have had him taken to the nearest prison for examination and closure, to be dealt with by law.

sentences.zh: 如法所稱，暅卽主。

translations.literal: As the law provides, Xuan is the principal offender.
translations.idiomatic: As the law provides, Xuan is the principal offender.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案：豫章內史臣伏暅，含疵表行，藉悖成心，語默一違，資敬兼盡。

translations.literal: I respectfully charge: Internal Magistrate of Yuzhang, minister Fu Xuan, bearing flaws that mark his conduct, leaning on perversity as his heart; in speech and silence alike he violated duty, exhausting what should be reverence.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully charge: internal magistrate of Yuzhang, minister Fu Xuan, whose flaws mark his conduct and whose perversity has become his heart; in speech and silence alike he violated duty and exhausted all reverence owed.

sentences.zh: 幸屬昌時，擢以不次。

translations.literal: Fortunate to live in a flourishing age, he was promoted out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunate to live in a flourishing age, he was promoted out of turn.

sentences.zh: 溪壑可盈，志欲無滿。

translations.literal: Ravines and gullies can be filled, yet ambition and desire know no satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Ravines and gullies can be filled, yet ambition and desire know no limit.

sentences.zh: 要君東走，豈曰止足之歸；

translations.literal: Importuning his lord to flee east—can this be called the return of knowing when to stop?
translations.idiomatic: Importuning his lord to flee east—can this be called knowing when to stop?

sentences.zh: 負志解巾，異乎激處之致。

translations.literal: Bearing resentment to remove the towel—different from the reach of one stirred to withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing resentment while doffing office—far from the impulse that drives a man to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 甘此脂膏，孰非荼苦；

translations.literal: Savoring this fat and grease—what is not bitter thorn?
translations.idiomatic: Savoring this fat and grease—what is not bitter as thorn?

sentences.zh: 佩茲龜組，豈殊縲絏。

translations.literal: Wearing these turtle seals and silken cords—how is it different from hemp bonds?
translations.idiomatic: Wearing these turtle seals and silken cords—how is it different from hempen bonds?

sentences.zh: 宜明風憲，肅正簡書。

translations.literal: Wind and law should be made clear; the red bamboo registers should be sternly corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and law should be made clear; the red registers should be sternly corrected.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，請以見事免暅所居官，凡諸位任，一皆削除。

translations.literal: We counsellors jointly propose: on grounds of the present case remove Xuan from all offices held—every rank and appointment, delete entirely.
translations.idiomatic: We counsellors jointly propose: on grounds of the present case remove Xuan from all offices held—every rank and appointment, delete entirely.

sentences.zh: 有詔勿治，暅遂得就郡。

translations.literal: An edict came not to prosecute; Xuan thus took up the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict came not to prosecute; Xuan thus took up the commandery.

sentences.zh: 視事三年，徵爲給事黃門侍郎，領國子博士，未及起。

translations.literal: After three years in office he was summoned as Secretariat Attendant of the Yellow Gate and concurrent Erudite of the National University; before he could take up the appointment—
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he was summoned as Secretariat Attendant of the Yellow Gate and concurrent Erudite of the National University, but before he could take up the appointment—

sentences.zh: 普通元年，卒於郡，時年五十九。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong he died in the commandery, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putong he died in the commandery, aged fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射徐勉爲之墓誌，其一章曰：「東區南服，愛結民胥，相望伏闕，繼軌奏書。
