translations.literal: Right Vice Minister of Works Xu Mian wrote his tomb inscription; one section reads: "In the eastern districts and southern realm, affection bound officials and people; crowding the gate in prostration, one after another they memorialized in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Minister of Works Xu Mian wrote his tomb inscription; one section reads: "In the eastern districts and southern realm, affection bound officials and people; crowding the gate in prostration, one after another they memorialized in writing.

sentences.zh: 或臥其轍，或扳其車，或圖其像，或式其閭。

translations.literal: Some lay on his carriage tracks, some pulled at his cart, some painted his likeness, some bowed at his lane."
translations.idiomatic: Some lay across his carriage tracks, some pulled at his cart, some painted his likeness, some bowed at his lane."

sentences.zh: 思耿借寇，曷以尚諸。」

translations.literal: Longing for Geng and borrowing Kou—how can this be surpassed?"
translations.idiomatic: Longing for Geng and borrowing Kou—how can this be surpassed?"

sentences.zh: 初，暅父曼容與樂安任瑤皆匿於齊太尉王儉，瑤子昉及暅並見知。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xuan's father Manrong and Ren Yao of Lean both found shelter with Qi Grand Marshal Wang Jian; Yao's son Fang and Xuan were both recognized.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xuan's father Manrong and Ren Yao of Lean both found shelter with Qi Grand Marshal Wang Jian; Yao's son Fang and Xuan were both recognized.

sentences.zh: 頃之，昉才遇稍盛，齊末，昉已爲司徒右長史，暅猶滯於參軍事；

translations.literal: Before long Fang's talent and favor grew; by the end of Qi, Fang was already Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education while Xuan still languished as a staff officer;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fang's talent and favor grew; by the end of Qi, Fang was already right chief clerk of the Minister of Education while Xuan still languished as a staff officer;

sentences.zh: 及其終也，名位略相侔。

translations.literal: yet when Fang died, name and rank were roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: yet when Fang died, name and rank were roughly equal.

sentences.zh: 暅性儉素，車服粗惡，外雖退靜，內不免心競，故見譏於時。

translations.literal: Xuan was frugal and plain by nature; carriage and dress were coarse and poor; outwardly he seemed withdrawn and calm, inwardly he could not escape rivalry of heart—hence ridicule in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was frugal and plain by nature; carriage and dress were coarse; outwardly withdrawn and calm, inwardly he could not escape rivalry—hence ridicule in his day.

sentences.zh: 能推薦後來，常若不及，少年士子，或以此依之。

translations.literal: He could recommend those who came after, as if always falling short; young scholar-officials sometimes relied on him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He could recommend those who came after, as if always falling short; young scholar-officials sometimes relied on him for this.

sentences.zh: 何遠字義方，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: He Yuan, styled Yifang, was a man of Tan in Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He Yuan, styled Yifang, came from Tan in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 父慧炬，齊尚書郎。

translations.literal: His father Huiju was Qi Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huiju was Qi Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 遠釋褐江夏王國侍郎，轉奉朝請。

translations.literal: Yuan began his career as Gentleman of the Kingdom of Jiangxia and transferred to Respite at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan began as Gentleman of the Kingdom of Jiangxia and transferred to Respite at Court.

sentences.zh: 永元中，江夏王寶玄於京口爲護軍將軍崔慧景所奉，入圍宮城，遠豫其事。

translations.literal: In Yongyuan, Prince of Jiangxia Bao Xuan at Jingkou was backed by Guard General Cui Huijing and entered to besiege the palace city; Yuan took part in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan, Prince of Jiangxia Bao Xuan at Jingkou was backed by Guard General Cui Huijing and entered to besiege the palace city; Yuan took part.

sentences.zh: 事敗，乃亡抵長沙宣武王，王深保匿焉。

translations.literal: When the affair failed, he fled to Prince of Changsha, the Xuanwu King, who deeply protected and hid him.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair failed, he fled to the Xuanwu King, Prince of Changsha, who deeply protected and hid him.

sentences.zh: 遠求得桂陽王融保藏之，旣而發覺，收捕者至，遠逾垣以免；

translations.literal: Yuan found Prince of Guiyang Wang Rong to shelter him; when this was discovered and arresters came, Yuan scaled a wall and escaped;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan found Prince of Guiyang Wang Rong to shelter him; when this was discovered and arresters came, Yuan scaled a wall and escaped;

sentences.zh: 融及遠家人皆見執，融遂遇禍，遠家屬繫尚方。

translations.literal: Rong and Yuan's family were all seized; Rong met disaster, and Yuan's kin were held in the Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Yuan's family were all seized; Rong met disaster, and Yuan's kin were held in the Imperial Workshop.

sentences.zh: 遠亡渡江，使其故人高江產共聚衆，欲迎高祖義師，東昏黨聞之，使捕遠等，衆復潰散。

translations.literal: Yuan fled across the river and had his old acquaintance Gao Jiangchan gather men to welcome Gaozu's righteous army; Donghun's faction heard and sent to capture Yuan and the rest—the crowd scattered again.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan fled across the river and had his old acquaintance Gao Jiangchan gather men to welcome Gaozu's righteous army; Donghun's faction heard and sent to capture them—the crowd scattered again.

sentences.zh: 遠因降魏，入壽陽，見刺史王肅，欲同義舉，肅不能用，乃求迎高祖，肅許之。

translations.literal: Yuan then surrendered to Wei, entered Shouyang, saw Inspector Wang Su, wished to join in righteous action; Su could not employ him, so he asked to welcome Gaozu—Su consented.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan then surrendered to Wei, entered Shouyang, and saw Inspector Wang Su, wishing to join in righteous action; Su could not employ him, so he asked to welcome Gaozu—and Su consented.

sentences.zh: 遣兵援送，得達高祖。

translations.literal: Su sent troops to escort him, and he reached Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Su sent troops to escort him, and he reached Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖見遠，謂張弘策曰：「何遠美丈夫，而能破家報舊德，未易及也。

translations.literal: Gaozu saw Yuan and said to Zhang Hongce: "He Yuan is a fine man—able to ruin his family to repay old kindness; not easy to match."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu saw Yuan and said to Zhang Hongce: "He Yuan is a fine man—able to ruin his family to repay old kindness; not easy to match."

sentences.zh: 」板輔國將軍，隨軍東下，旣破硃雀軍，以爲建康令。

translations.literal: He was provisionally made General Who Supports the State, followed the army east; after the Zhuzque army was broken, he was made Magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was provisionally made General Who Supports the State, followed the army east; after the Zhuzque army was broken, he was made magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，爲步兵校尉，以奉迎勳封廣興男，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, he was Colonel of the Footsoldiers; for merit in welcoming the throne he was enfeoffed as Baron of Guangxing, fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he was colonel of the Footsoldiers; for merit in welcoming the throne he was enfeoffed as Baron of Guangxing, fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷建武將軍、後軍鄱陽王恢錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Establishes Might and Recorder of the Rear Army under the Prince of Poyang, Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General Who Establishes Might and recorder of the rear army under Prince Hui of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 遠與恢素善，在府盡其志力，知無不爲，恢亦推心仗之，恩寄甚密。

translations.literal: Yuan and Hui had long been on good terms; in the princely office he exhausted his will and strength, leaving nothing undone; Hui too relied on him with open heart—favor and trust were very close.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Hui had long been on good terms; in the princely office he exhausted his will and strength, leaving nothing undone; Hui too relied on him with open heart—favor and trust were very close.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷武昌太守。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to administrator of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 遠本倜儻，尚輕俠，至是乃折節爲吏，杜絕交遊，饋遺秋毫無所受。

translations.literal: Yuan had been free and easy by nature, fond of light chivalry; now he restrained himself as an official, cut off social ties, and accepted not the slightest gift.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had been free and easy by nature, fond of light chivalry; now he restrained himself as an official, cut off social ties, and accepted not the slightest gift.

sentences.zh: 武昌俗皆汲江水，盛夏遠患水溫，每以錢買民井寒水；

translations.literal: Custom in Wuchang was to draw from the river; in high summer Yuan feared the warm water and always bought cold well water from commoners with cash;
translations.idiomatic: Custom in Wuchang was to draw from the river; in high summer Yuan feared the warm water and always bought cold well water from commoners with cash;

sentences.zh: 不取錢者，則摙水還之。

translations.literal: those who would not take money, he drew water for them in return.
translations.idiomatic: those who would not take money, he drew water for them in return.

sentences.zh: 其佗事率多如此。

translations.literal: Other matters were mostly like this.
translations.idiomatic: Other matters were mostly like this.

sentences.zh: 跡雖似偽，而能委曲用意焉。

translations.literal: The track may seem like artifice, yet he could bend and turn with thoughtful intent.
translations.idiomatic: The track may seem like artifice, yet he could bend and turn with thoughtful intent.

sentences.zh: 車服尤弊素，器物無銅漆。

translations.literal: Carriage and dress were especially worn and plain; utensils had no bronze or lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: Carriage and dress were especially worn and plain; utensils had no bronze or lacquer.

sentences.zh: 江左多水族，甚賤，遠每食不過幹魚數片而已。

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze has many aquatic foods, very cheap; Yuan's meals were no more than a few slices of dried fish.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze has many aquatic foods, very cheap; Yuan's meals were no more than a few slices of dried fish.

sentences.zh: 然性剛嚴，吏民多以細事受鞭罰者，遂爲人所訟，徵下廷尉，被劾數十條。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was hard and severe; officials and people often suffered whipping over small matters—thus someone sued him; he was summoned to the Minister of Justice and impeached on several dozen counts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature was hard and severe; officials and people often suffered whipping over small matters—thus someone sued him; he was summoned to the Minister of Justice and impeached on several dozen counts.

sentences.zh: 當時士大夫坐法，皆不受立，遠度己無贓，就立三七日不款，猶以私藏禁仗除名。

translations.literal: At the time when scholar-officials faced the law, none would stand for questioning; Yuan judged himself innocent of corruption, stood for inquiry, and for twenty-seven days made no confession—yet was still struck from the rolls for privately storing forbidden weapons.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when scholar-officials faced the law, none would stand for questioning; Yuan judged himself innocent of corruption, stood for inquiry, and for twenty-seven days made no confession—yet was still struck from the rolls for privately storing forbidden weapons.

sentences.zh: 後起爲鎮南將軍、武康令。

translations.literal: Later he was restored as staff officer to the General Who Pacifies the South and Magistrate of Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was restored as staff officer to the General Who Pacifies the South and magistrate of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 愈厲廉節，除淫祀，正身率職，民甚稱之。

translations.literal: He redoubled his integrity, eliminated illicit shrines, corrected his person and led his duty—the people praised him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He redoubled his integrity, eliminated illicit shrines, corrected his person and led his duty—the people praised him greatly.

sentences.zh: 太守王彬巡屬縣，諸縣盛供帳以待焉，至武康，遠獨設糗水而已。

translations.literal: Administrator Wang Bin toured subordinate counties; each county lavishly prepared provision tents to receive him—at Wukang, Yuan alone set out parched grain and water.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Wang Bin toured subordinate counties; each county lavishly prepared provision tents to receive him—at Wukang, Yuan alone set out parched grain and water.

sentences.zh: 彬去，遠送至境，進斗酒雙鵝爲別。

translations.literal: When Bin left, Yuan saw him to the border and offered a peck of wine and paired geese as farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin left, Yuan saw him to the border and offered a peck of wine and paired geese as farewell.

sentences.zh: 彬戲曰：「卿禮有過陸納，將不爲古人所笑乎？

translations.literal: Bin joked: "Your courtesy exceeds Lu Na's—will you not be laughed at by the men of old?"
translations.idiomatic: Bin joked: "Your courtesy exceeds Lu Na's—will you not be laughed at by the men of old?"

sentences.zh: 」高祖聞其能，擢爲宣城太守。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard of his ability and promoted him to Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu heard of his ability and promoted him to administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 自縣爲近畿大郡，近代未之有也。

translations.literal: From magistrate to a great near-capital commandery—nothing like it in recent times.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate to a great near-capital commandery—nothing like it in recent times.

sentences.zh: 郡經寇抄，遠盡心綏理，復著名迹。

translations.literal: The commandery had suffered raids and plunder; Yuan devoted himself to pacification and governance, again leaving notable traces.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had suffered raids and plunder; Yuan devoted himself to pacification and governance, again leaving notable traces.

sentences.zh: 朞年，遷樹功將軍、始興內史。

translations.literal: After one year he was transferred to General Who Establishes Merit and Internal Magistrate of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: After one year he was transferred to General Who Establishes Merit and internal magistrate of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 時泉陵侯淵朗爲桂州，緣道剽掠，入始興界，草木無所犯。

translations.literal: At the time Marquis of Quanling Yuan Lang held Guizhou; along the route he plundered—entering Shixing's borders, not even grass and trees were harmed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Marquis of Quanling Yuan Lang held Guizhou; along the route he plundered—entering Shixing's borders, not even grass and trees were harmed.

sentences.zh: 遠在官，好開途巷，修葺牆屋，民居市里，城隍廄庫，所過若營家焉。

translations.literal: While in office Yuan loved to open roads and lanes, repair walls and houses— dwelling quarters, market streets, city walls, stables and granaries—wherever he passed it was as if tending his own home.
translations.idiomatic: While in office Yuan loved to open roads and lanes, repair walls and houses— dwelling quarters, market streets, city walls, stables and granaries—wherever he passed it was as if tending his own home.

sentences.zh: 田秩俸錢，並無所取，歲暮，擇民尤窮者，充其租調，以此爲常。

translations.literal: Field salary and stipend cash he took none of; at year's end he chose the poorest commoners and paid their tax levies—this became his custom.
translations.idiomatic: Field salary and stipend cash he took none of; at year's end he chose the poorest commoners and paid their tax levies—this became his custom.

sentences.zh: 然其聽訟猶人，不能過絕，而性果斷，民不敢非，畏而惜之。

translations.literal: Yet in hearing cases he was like other men, unable to go beyond that; but his nature was resolute and sharp—people did not dare find fault, fearing yet cherishing him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in hearing cases he was like other men, unable to go beyond that; but his nature was resolute and sharp—people did not dare find fault, fearing yet cherishing him.

sentences.zh: 所至皆生爲立祠，表言治狀，高祖每優詔答焉。

translations.literal: Wherever he went, while he still lived shrines were built; memorials reported his governance—Gaozu each time replied with gracious edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went, while he still lived shrines were built; memorials reported his governance—Gaozu each time replied with gracious edicts.

sentences.zh: 天監十六年，詔曰：「何遠前在武康，已著廉平；

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Tianjian an edict said: "He Yuan earlier at Wukang already showed pure fairness;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Tianjian an edict said: "He Yuan earlier at Wukang already showed pure fairness;

sentences.zh: 復蒞二邦，彌盡清白。

translations.literal: again governing two commanderies, he has ever more fully shown unsullied integrity.
translations.idiomatic: again governing two commanderies, he has ever more fully shown unsullied integrity.

sentences.zh: 政先治道，惠留民愛，雖古之良二千石，無以過也。

translations.literal: He puts governance before all, leaves kindness and keeps the people's love— even the good two-thousand-bushel officials of old cannot surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: He puts governance before all, leaves kindness and keeps the people's love— even the good two-thousand-bushel officials of old cannot surpass this.

sentences.zh: 宜升內榮，以顯外績。

translations.literal: Inner honor should be raised to display outer achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Inner honor should be raised to display outer achievement.

sentences.zh: 可給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Let him be Attendant of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be Attendant of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 」遠卽還，仍爲仁威長史。

translations.literal: Yuan returned at once and became Chief Clerk to the General of Humane Might.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan returned at once and became chief clerk to the General of Humane Might.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出爲信武將軍，監吳郡。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as General of Trustworthy Might and Supervisor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went out as General of Trustworthy Might and supervisor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 在吳頗有酒失，遷東陽太守。

translations.literal: While in Wu he had several lapses involving drink; he was transferred to Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu he had several lapses with wine; he was transferred to administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 遠處職，疾強富如仇讎，視貧細如子弟，特爲豪右所畏憚。

translations.literal: In office Yuan hated the powerful and wealthy as if they were mortal enemies; he treated the poor and lowly as his own children and sons, and the local gentry especially feared and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: In office Yuan hated the rich and powerful like mortal foes and treated the poor like his own kin—the gentry especially feared him.

sentences.zh: 在東陽歲餘，復爲受罰者所謗，坐免歸。

translations.literal: After slightly more than a year in Dongyang, he was again slandered by those he had punished; convicted on the charges, he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: After a year in Dongyang, those he had punished slandered him again; convicted, he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 遠耿介無私曲，居人間，絕請謁，不造詣。

translations.literal: Yuan was upright and incorruptible; living among men, he cut off all petitions and visits and never paid calls on others.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and free of private bias, Yuan cut off petitions and visits and never called on others.

sentences.zh: 與貴賤書疏，抗禮如一。

translations.literal: In letters to high and low alike, he observed equal courtesy throughout.
translations.idiomatic: In letters to high and low alike, he kept equal courtesy.

sentences.zh: 其所會遇，未嘗以顏色下人，以此多爲俗士所惡。

translations.literal: In every encounter he never softened his bearing toward others—and for this vulgar men often despised him.
translations.idiomatic: He never softened his manner toward anyone he met—and vulgar men often despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 其清公實爲天下第一。

translations.literal: His integrity and fairness were truly unrivaled under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity was truly unrivaled under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 居數郡，見可欲終不變其心，妻子饑寒，如下貧者。

translations.literal: Though he governed several commanderies, whenever tempting gain came within sight he never changed in heart; wife and children knew hunger and cold like the poorest of men.
translations.idiomatic: Though he governed several commanderies, tempting gain never changed his heart; wife and children knew hunger and cold like the poorest men.

sentences.zh: 及去東陽歸家，經年歲口不言榮辱，士類益以此多之。

translations.literal: When he left Dongyang and returned home, year after year he never spoke of honor or disgrace—and scholars all the more admired him for it.
translations.idiomatic: When he left Dongyang for home, year after year he never spoke of honor or disgrace—and scholars admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 其輕財好義，周人之急，言不虛妄，蓋天性也。

translations.literal: He was lightly attached to wealth yet loved righteousness, rushing to relieve others in distress; his words were never hollow or false—this was surely his nature.
translations.idiomatic: He scorned wealth yet loved righteousness, rushed to help the desperate, and never spoke falsely—it was his nature.

sentences.zh: 每戲語人云：「卿能得我一妄語，則謝卿以一縑。

translations.literal: He would often jestingly tell people: "If you can get one false word from me, I'll thank you with a bolt of silk."
translations.idiomatic: He often jested: "Get one false word from me and I'll thank you with a bolt of silk."

sentences.zh: 」衆共伺之，不能記也。

translations.literal: The crowd all watched for it—they could never record a single instance.
translations.idiomatic: All watched for it—they never caught a single false word.

sentences.zh: 後復起爲征西諮議參軍、中撫司馬。

translations.literal: Later he was again raised to Staff Counselor of the Pacifying West and Army Aide of the Central Pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was raised again as staff counselor of the Pacifying West and army aide of the Central Pacification.

sentences.zh: 普通二年，卒，時年五十二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong he died, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Putong he died, aged fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 高祖厚贈賜之。

translations.literal: Gaozu bestowed rich posthumous gifts on him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu bestowed rich posthumous gifts on him.

translations.literal: Commentary section marker in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: Marker denoting the historian's commentary section in the source text.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：前史有循吏，何哉？

translations.literal: Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel of Chen, said: Earlier histories had chapters on "Orderly Officials"—what was that about?
translations.idiomatic: Yao Cha, Chen Minister of Personnel, said: Earlier histories had chapters on orderly officials—why?

sentences.zh: 世使然也。

translations.literal: The age made it so.
translations.idiomatic: The age made it so.

sentences.zh: 漢武役繁姦起，循平不能，故有苛酷誅戮以勝之，亦多怨濫矣。

translations.literal: Under Han Wudi corvée labor grew heavy and corruption rose; orderly governance could not contain it, so harsh punishments and executions were wielded to overcome the tide—yet much resentment and excess followed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han Wudi corvée grew heavy and corruption rose; orderly rule could not cope, so harsh punishments and executions were used—and much resentment and excess followed.

sentences.zh: 梁興，破觚爲圓，斵雕爲樸，教民以孝悌，勸之以農桑，於是桀黠化爲由余，輕薄變爲忠厚。

translations.literal: When Liang rose, square corners were rounded and ornament pared to plainness; the people were taught filial piety and sibling duty and urged toward farming and sericulture—until fierce and cunning men turned into men like You Yu, and the frivolous became steadfast and honest.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang rose, corners were rounded and ornament stripped to plainness; the people were taught filial piety and urged toward farming and sericulture—fierce and cunning men became like You Yu, the frivolous turned steadfast.

sentences.zh: 淳風已洽，民自知禁。

translations.literal: Pure custom had spread; the people knew restraint on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Pure custom had spread; the people knew restraint on their own.

sentences.zh: 堯舜之民，比屋可封，信矣。

translations.literal: The people of Yao and Shun—a home behind every door worthy of being sealed with praise—this was indeed credible.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yao and Shun, a sealed home behind every door—this was indeed true.

sentences.zh: 若夫酷吏，於梁無取焉。

translations.literal: As for cruel officials—Liang had no need of them.
translations.idiomatic: As for cruel officials—Liang had no need of them.
